name: vornik-companion
description: Async-offload companion for Claude Code with project RAG memory + per-repo scoping (migration 75). Delegate reviews / audits / validations / research / bulk-ingest; recall + remember scoped to the current repo so one project's RAG can serve multiple repos without cross-pollution. SessionStart digest surfaces completed delegations and recent memory updates. /upload attaches local files to delegations as base64 INPUT artifacts without burning client tokens; /rag-ingest (0.4.2) is the dedicated bulk-ingest entry point for project RAG memory (supports directories + --tag). 0.4.5: hotfix — session-start.sh now emits the v2-style {hookSpecificOutput,hookEventName,additionalContext} JSON envelope so the digest renders in the Claude Code v2.1+ welcome banner. Pre-0.4.5 raw markdown reached the model's context but was silently dropped from the banner. 0.4.4 wired hooks.json; 0.4.5 makes the wired script speak the v2 protocol. 0.4.6: /rag-ingest gained an explicit per-file size cap (--max-file-bytes, default 512 KiB) + accurate docs after the companion-rag-ingest WORKFLOW was fixed to copy staged sources with run_shell (cp/cat) instead of re-emitting bytes via file_read→file_write — the latter silently failed on large files (260 KiB CHANGELOG). Companion swarm template now also ships the rag-ingester role. 0.4.7: repo-scope resolvers (session-start.sh + /upload + /rag-ingest) now fall back to the current folder basename when there's no git origin / not a git repo, instead of returning empty — an empty scope surfaced to the operator as context "none" and silently routed recall/remember/delegate project-wide. All three resolvers stay in lockstep. 0.4.8: delegate guidance hardened after the 2026-06-05 silent-skip incident — file paths in a delegate prompt are never uploaded; daemon-side require_input_artifacts now rejects artifact-less rag-ingest delegations, and the delegate command/skill docs steer to /rag-ingest + /upload. 0.4.9: /rag-ingest docs updated for the 2026-06-11 server-side rewrite — companion-rag-ingest is now DETERMINISTIC and agent-free: the workflow has no agent step and the executor ingests staged input artifacts directly by ID (ingest_input_artifacts), removing the weak rag-ingester LLM from the copy loop that repeatedly claimed produced_files it never wrote (the 'try a different tool' large-file ingest failures). File size and model quality no longer affect whether the copy lands. 0.4.10: companion-architectural-review workflow now reviews the STAGED input artifact as its source of truth and refuses to review project memory (RAG holds stale/multiple doc revisions → contradictory findings); /upload is documented as workflow-generic and the canonical doc-review path (`/upload companion-architectural-review "…" <file>`); the delegate skill + /review + /delegate docs steer clients to attach files via /upload for any file-bearing workflow rather than naming a path in a delegate prompt the agent container can't read. 0.5.0: BREAKING command rename — dropped the redundant vornik- prefix from plugin actions (/vornik-upload→/upload, /vornik-rag-ingest→/rag-ingest, skill vornik-delegate→delegate); the plugin namespace already conveys vornik-companion, so vornik-companion:vornik-upload was doubly redundant. Usage guidance strengthened to make companion-architectural-review the default MERGE GATE for non-trivial changes and design docs: commit, upload the diff (git diff base...branch > file) or design doc as a staged artifact via /upload, block on the verdict, fix every Critical/Important finding, re-review, then merge; single-quote /upload prompts with NO double-quotes or backticks (they break the bash wrapper); delegate long reviews/audits/research proactively at task start. 0.6.0: new /memory-correct command + memory_correct MCP tool — soft-refute a wrong/stale RAG fact (top hybrid-search matches flip to validation_status='refuted' and drop out of recall) and optionally store the correction as a verified chunk; the programmatic equivalent of the dispatcher's chat-side memory_correct, so a host LLM can make newer findings take precedence over superseded notes (requires a memory_write-scoped key). ALSO: /remember rewritten to the heredoc→file→json.dumps→POST pattern (same hardening /upload and /rag-ingest already use) so long notes with quotes/backticks/newlines/em-dashes land intact instead of being mangled or truncated by inline MCP tool-call serialization; /remember and /memory-correct both gained leading --scope/--class/--ttl (remember) and --max/--scope (memory-correct) flags. 0.7.0: /memory-correct + the memory_correct MCP tool gain a surgical by-id mode — pass one or more --chunk-id (chunk_ids[] over MCP, from a prior /recall) to refute exactly those chunks instead of the claim-search top matches. Needed because once an authoritative correction exists it out-ranks the stale chunk in a claim search, so claim-mode would demote the correction rather than the stale note; by-id targets the right chunk. wrong_claim and chunk_ids are now either-or. 0.8.0: knowledge-skill commands — /skill-propose, /skill-search, /skill-get, /skill-list, /skill-approve, /skill-reject wrap the new daemon-owned knowledge-skill MCP verbs (instructional SKILL.md-style know-how, distinct from SWARM-SKILL.md capability skills and from RAG memory). A proposed skill lands as a draft and only fires after an operator with a skill_admin key approves it; approved skills are served to swarm roles + every companion client. Gated by new per-key caps: skill_read (search/get/list), skill_write (propose), skill_admin (approve/reject) — grant via `vornikctl companion grant --skill-read/--skill-write/--skill-admin/--skill-all`. 0.9.0: knowledge-skill auto-authoring — the SessionStart hook now plants a directive telling the model to capture durable, reusable, project-relevant procedures it works out during the session as DRAFT skills via skill_propose (dedupe via skill_search first; drafts need operator approval before they activate). Vornik never sees the transcript — only the resulting skill_propose call. Pairs with the existing /skill-* commands and the maturity engine (usage-driven promote/decay of approved skills). 0.10.0: cross-project (global) skills — /skill-set-global <id> [global|project] and a `global` arg on /skill-propose flip a skill's reach so an approved skill injects into EVERY project's roles (not just its home project) — the way a procedure captured in your companion project reaches the janka/assistant autonomy roles. Both are skill_admin-gated and project-checked; global drafts are labelled 'affects ALL projects' on every review surface (Telegram/UI). Operator equivalents: `vornikctl knowledge set-global/set-project` and the Admin → Skills inbox buttons. 0.11.0: RAG-first default — the SessionStart hook now plants a directive telling the assistant to `recall` BEFORE reading code on design/architecture/roadmap/"how does X work" questions (and bug symptoms that look like a known incident), treating the design/spec/decision-class LLDs in project memory as the authoritative design record and reading code only to verify a named symbol still matches. The rule used to live only in the operator's per-user CLAUDE.md, so it didn't ship with the plugin or help other operators. It is a PREFERENCE (trivial literal grep/cat lookups skip it) with a class-scoped trust boundary (research/incident/companion notes are hypotheses, not fact — so a poisoned chunk from a failed task isn't asserted as truth). The recall MCP tool Description gained the same steering clause behind a `| USAGE:` separator, so Codex (which has no SessionStart hook) gets the signal too. 0.12.0: new `report-problem` skill bundled with the plugin — teaches the companion how to help a user file an anonymized Vornik problem report (bug, crash, misbehaving swarm, or INSTALL failure) as a prefilled github.com/grinco/vornik issue, throughout the product lifecycle. The heavy lifting is the deterministic `vornikctl report` CLI (daemon-up rich diagnostics, `--offline` static checks, `--dry-run`/`--url-only`), plus the quickstart.sh installer's own EXIT-trap failure URL for pre-daemon install errors. The skill is the guardrail: review-the-anonymized-body-before-submit, zero-auth (user files under their own GitHub identity, nothing auto-posted), and the support-bundle attachment caveat. Two-tier anonymization (secret redaction + a public scrubber stripping emails / whole home+tilde paths / all IPv4 / this host's name) with fail-closed semantics. 0.13.0: delegate guidance corrected for the T-8f69 staging fix (2026-07-25). The daemon now DERIVES skip_auto_extract from a workflow's require_input_artifacts — on both the companion delegate and the REST create-task path — so a plain delegate() carrying inputArtifacts to companion-architectural-review / companion-doc-review / companion-rag-ingest is safe: the raw file is staged for the agent instead of being auto-extracted into RAG at upload time, and the client no longer has to remember the flag. Previously these docs never mentioned skip_auto_extract at all, so an artifact-bearing review delegated without it got inputExtractions stamped on the task, which SUPPRESSED file staging; the reviewer role (allowedTools is builtins-only, no document_* MCP tools) then hit 403 FORBIDDEN 17 times and reviewed 6 partial RAG chunks instead of the attached document. /upload keeps its explicit skip_auto_extract=True — never downgraded, and still correct against an older daemon. 0.14.0: operator lifecycle triad — two new skills, `configure-vornik` and `troubleshoot-vornik`, join the shipped `report-problem` so configuring, diagnosing, and reporting are each a guarded path over the deterministic vornikctl surface rather than an improvisation. configure-vornik leads with the config-resolution hazards that silently no-op an otherwise correct change: the registry tree (projects/+swarms/+workflows/) is resolved by a FALLBACK CHAIN, not a single env var, and the daemon's chain differs from vornikctl's (vornikctl also tries ~/.config/vornik/configs and /etc/vornik/configs; both end at a relative `configs` taken from the process's cwd). VORNIK_CONFIGS_DIR is honoured only if the directory ALREADY has all three subdirs — otherwise it is skipped with no error and resolution falls through, which is the usual cause of "my env var is set but it reads the wrong tree". `vornikctl init` resolves against the invoking shell, not the daemon unit, so on a non-default install it can write a valid file into a tree the daemon never reads. The skill also pins the apply loop (doctor → config reload → config reload-status, where validation errors actually surface), secrets as ${ENV_VAR} never literals, and that systemd resolves BOTH Environment= and EnvironmentFile= at ExecStart only — so unit changes need a restart, and a clean env_file_freshness does NOT mean the environment is fresh because Environment= edits have no check at all. troubleshoot-vornik routes by symptom: daemon-down → `doctor --offline` (with the caveat that it resolves paths from your shell, not the dead daemon, and has no flag to pin them); degraded → `doctor` / `doctor feature`; failed task → task get/explain/tail then `playbook show <CLASS>`; change-didn't-take → reload-status; object missing entirely → the whole registry tree failed to resolve. It states that --fix repairs only the eight operational findings and that schema, runtime, security-posture, pricing, and budget checks are diagnostic only, and it exits to report-problem when the ladder bottoms out. Both skills are mirrored into the codex-companion bundle. 0.15.0: new `whoami` MCP tool + `/whoami` command — repo_scope is resolved per-call server-side (an explicit arg, else the key's default_repo_scope), never held as session state, so there was no way to ask "what RAG project/scope are MY calls using right now" once the SessionStart digest (which only fires once, at session open) scrolled out of context. whoami() returns project_id, client_kind, session_label, default_repo_scope, and effective_repo_scope (optionally previewed against a candidate repo_scope arg). No new permission gate — it echoes the key's own bound metadata, same posture as catalog(). 0.15.1: README accuracy only, no behaviour change — "What you get" still claimed 9 MCP tools and 7 slash commands (true around 0.4.x; actually 19 and 18 as of 0.15.0), so a bundle that had just gained whoami was advertising a surface three phases out of date. It now names the real task / RAG / knowledge-skill tool sets and points at /help as the authority, so the count cannot rot again. 0.15.2: hotfix for a fresh macOS install — session-start.sh failed to parse under bash 3.2 (still /bin/bash on macOS) with "line 333: unexpected EOF while looking for matching", so the SessionStart digest never ran. bash 3.2 scans for the closing paren of $( ) WITHOUT honoring heredoc bodies, so an apostrophe in the prose of the skill-authoring and RAG-first directives was read as an opening quote; both heredocs are now wrapped in functions. bash 4+ parses the old shape fine, which is why local `bash -n` and shellcheck both passed it — the hook is now in the linted set and scripts/check-bash32-heredoc.sh fails the build on the pattern. ALSO: /whoami told the model nothing about output formatting and it emitted ` ` to align columns, which the terminal renders literally; the command now says plain markdown, one fact per line. Its description of default_repo_scope as a "floor" is corrected to a fallback — an explicit per-call repo_scope always wins. 0.16.0: new `report_problem` MCP verb + report-problem skill guidance for it. A companion user whose daemon runs on ANOTHER host could not file a problem report at all: the skill drives `vornikctl report` locally and there was no MCP path, so same-host installs worked and remote ones silently had no route. The verb returns a review URL and the anonymized body from the SAME builder the chat tool uses, which collects NOTHING from the daemon host — no doctor findings, no journal tail — because no remotely-reachable path may execute a program (operator ruling 2026-08-03). Thinner than the CLI's report by design; richer diagnostics still require an operator running the CLI on the host. Nothing is submitted: the body is destined for a PUBLIC repo, so the user reads it and presses submit under their own identity. 0.17.0: new `validate-install` skill, and a published reference architecture for it to measure against (docs.vornik.io/reference/reference-architecture/). The lifecycle triad could configure, diagnose and report, but had no answer to "is this install set up correctly?" — a question that arrives at handover and after upgrades, with no symptom for troubleshoot-vornik to route on. The skill's discipline is configured-vs-observed: a config value is a statement of intent, never evidence of behaviour, so every check reads the daemon's RESOLVED state (the boot log) and then the ledger that proves it ran. The canonical case is ours — reranker.enabled true, reranker wired, and never fired across a six-figure count of recorded model calls because the request path dropped the per-request flag; config said yes and nothing reported the gap. Strictly read-only, and that constraint has teeth: POST /api/v1/config/reload looks like the natural way to ask whether the registry is valid and answers by APPLYING the tree, so an audit could push a half-edited file into service and cause the outage it was sent to find — the skill uses GET config/reload-status throughout. Severity is split three ways because the failure mode of a validator is noise: seven defect classes, five informational, and three never-report — names (installs are named for their history, and a name that reads like a test database is frequently the production one), model choices (heterogeneous models across roles is the intended design), and anything from a secrets tree. Mirrored into the codex-companion bundle. ALSO in 0.17.0: a `vornik-docs` skill teaching the host where the documentation lives, carrying the real site map (every path verified against docs/public) and an explicit order of preference: the installed CLI's own --help first, then a local checkout, then docs.vornik.io, and the model's own memory LAST — used to decide where to look, never as the answer. It exists because the characteristic failure when answering Vornik questions is a confident, plausible, nonexistent config key or CLI flag, and that failure is expensive: unknown keys are frequently ignored, so the user gets no error and the setting silently does nothing. The skill also states where the docs deliberately stop — internal design docs are unpublished, edition differences can look like docs gaps, and sizing numbers are absent by design — so an honest gap is reported instead of filled in. 0.17.1: configure-vornik gained the `VORNIK_API_URL` trap. vornikctl resolves its target daemon from VORNIK_API_URL and falls back to http://localhost:8080 when unset — which on a single-host deployment IS the production daemon, so a command aimed at a test instance lands on production instead. Read-only commands then return production's data (looking merely wrong) and a mutating one like `companion grant` succeeds there if the project name exists. Hit while running a benchmark against a second local daemon: VORNIK_URL was set (the variable companion/bench clients read) and the CLI silently kept its own default, querying production for a project that only existed on the bench instance. It 404'd only because production had no project by that name. Neither variable was documented anywhere before this. 0.18.0: new `/backlog-deposit` command + the shipped `scripts/vornik-backlog-deposit.sh` it drives — capture an off-scope finding into THIS repository's own backlog without derailing the task in hand. The process rule (find a defect outside your scope, file it, keep going) was unenforceable from a companion session: the daemon-side backlog_deposit tool is reachable only by an agent inside a vornik task, so operator-side sessions hand-edited BACKLOG.md and lost the two guards that make a deposit safe. This is deliberately CLIENT-side, and the daemon-side tool was evaluated and rejected for the job on two structural grounds: it renders one whitespace-flattened line capped at 600 characters (measured against this repo's backlog, the median item is ~1,800 chars and 47 of 48 exceed the cap, so the tables and code references that make an item actionable are exactly what is destroyed), and it writes a daemon-managed workspace — the daemon must not write the operator's checkout, so a deposit would land where nobody reads and need a manual promotion step. The client already owns the checkout, so writing it here is not a containment question at all. The script restores both lost guards: DEDUP against every existing item, understanding both grammars the file uses (`## [ ] P2 — Title (date)` headings and `- [ ] **Bold lead.**` bullets, taking the bold lead as the title), ignoring priority tags and trailing dates, and matching `[x]` done items so completed work is not re-filed; and a SECRET SCAN over title, body and evidence, because the backlog is committed and pushed and a credential in an evidence field is a rotation. Body arrives on stdin so structure — paragraphs, tables, code references — is preserved. Inserts only, never rewrites, and lands after the last top-level item rather than at EOF (this file ends in prose sections that would bury a finding). Exit codes: 3 duplicate, 4 secret refused, 5 no backlog found. Mirrored byte-identically into the codex-companion bundle, with a parity test that fails the build on drift.
